note: XVII asylum arrival redrawn in the Book I gothic manner (Ian, 16 Nov).
style: A dark gothic oil painting of 1893 in the manner of the reference: academic realism, deep chiaroscuro, brooding storm light, heavy shadow, a sense of dread. One single painting filling the whole 16:9 frame, no text, signature, border or black bars.

beats.text: Exterior, late on a stormy autumn afternoon in 1893: a closed carriage drawn by two dark horses halts before the tall iron gates of a lunatic asylum in the Essex marshes. A high black wall runs off into the gloom; beyond the gates the grim bulk of the asylum, many barred windows, one or two dimly lit; gnarled bare trees bending in the wind; a low, bruised sky with a last band of cold light on the horizon; wet gravel, a lamp beside the gate. The two passengers are small, unseen inside the carriage; the coachman hunched on the box.
